papers.title: Cycles on the universal moduli of rank 2 bundles over the hyperelliptic locus
papers.abstract: We establish a strong Franchetta property for the universal moduli stack of rank two vector bundles over smooth hyperelliptic curves and identify the image of the Chow ring in the cohomology of a fiber via restriction and the cycle class map as precisely the monodromy invariant cohomology classes. More precisely, for every genus $g\geq 2$, degree $d$, and hyperelliptic curve $C$ of genus $g$, we show that the restriction and the cycle class map identifies the Chow ring of the universal moduli stack with the subring of $H^* (Bun_{2,d}(C),\mathbb Q)$ generated by twisted $\kappa$-classes, which coincides with $H^{*}(Bun_{2,d}(C), \mathbb Q)^{\pi_1(\mathcal H_g,[C])}$. We use this viewpoint to give an alternative proof to a theorem of Larson in (arXiv:2404.12607), and verify a conjecture of the second author in (arXiv:2604.11958) in the rank $2$ case.

papers.title: P = W conjectures for varieties with nilpotent fundamental group
papers.abstract: We prove the cohomological and the geometric $P=W$ conjectures for the moduli spaces of $G$-Higgs bundles and $G$-local systems on any smooth complex projective variety $X$ with nilpotent fundamental group, and any connected complex reductive group $G$. To the best of our knowledge, our results provide the first instances of $P=W$ conjectures beyond curves and abelian varieties. Finally, we provide examples of our theorem for classical groups: as a byproduct of this analysis we investigate when symplectic resolutions of the corresponding character varieties exist.

papers.title: Character variety of the punctured sphere and the determinantal variety
papers.abstract: We show that the SL(2;C) character variety of the n-punctured sphere is described via the determinantal variety defined by an n x n symmetric matrix of rank at most 4 whose entries are the traces of simple closed curves on the surface. This result generalizes the Fricke-Klein-Vogt relations to arbitrary n, and we determine the structure of the kernel of the associated matrix.

papers.title: Polynomial twisted periods and affine vertex algebras
papers.abstract: We prove the conjecture of Kang, Lawrie, and Song that Zhu's $C_2$-algebra of a simply-laced boundary admissible affine vertex algebra is isomorphic to the Jacobian ring of an invariant potential obtained by lifting a polynomial twisted period from a Cartan subalgebra via the Chevalley isomorphism. We further identify the $C_2$-algebras of the corresponding Drinfeld-Sokolov reductions with the Jacobian rings of the restrictions of this potential to Slodowy slices. We also extend the Jacobian presentation to non-simply-laced principal boundary admissible affine vertex algebras, where the restriction of the potential to the Cartan subalgebra satisfies a Dunkl-singularity equation with root-length-dependent multiplicities.

papers.title: Counting Matrices of Prescribed Jordan Type in Incidence Algebras
papers.abstract: We count nilpotent matrices in the incidence algebra of a finite poset over a finite field that belong to a prescribed conjugacy class for the adjoint action of the general linear group. We prove that these counts depend only on the comparability graph of the poset. We introduce shuffle-prefix posets, a class containing all finite interval orders, and give explicit formulas for their nilpotent Jordan counts. These counts are polynomials with integer coefficients in the field size, valid over every finite field. Finally, Fourier duality relates conjugacy-class counts in a coordinate subspace to those in the subspace supported on the complementary matrix positions, whenever one subspace consists entirely of nilpotent matrices.

papers.title: Ice and mirrors
papers.abstract: Given a mirror pair of smooth affine principal upper cluster varieties admitting reddening sequences, we show that homological mirror symmetry for principal cluster varieties -- assumed compatible with certain cluster structures -- descends under freezing. This allows us to induct on the following class. A skew-symmetrizable matrix is peelable if, by mutations and removing sinks or sources, it can be reduced to the empty matrix; it is sub-peelable if it is a principal submatrix of a peelable matrix. We establish homological mirror symmetry for full rank upper cluster varieties whose mutable matrix is sub-peelable. We show sub-peelability for the Fock--Goncharov SL(n) quiver for any compact surface with nonempty boundary, all of whose boundaries have markings. Consequently, we establish homological mirror symmetry between the moduli of decorated SL(n) local systems and the corresponding pinned PGL(n) spaces. The results were obtained using ChatGPT Astra.

papers.title: An analogue of irreducible cuspidal representations for the group $PGL(2)$ over a two-dimensional local field
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a local non-archimedian field of odd residue characteristic and let $G=PGL(2)$. In this paper we study an analog of irreducible cuspidal representations of the group $G(F)$ when $F$ is replaced by the field $K=F((t))$. The story turns out to be similar to the classical case, but also with some differences. We present a construction of such representations essentially (up to a small subtlety) starting from a quadratic extension $L$ of $K$ and a character $\theta:L^*/K^*\to \mathbb C^*$ which is not Galois invariant. We also show that the restriction of the representations we construct to the group $P(K)$ (here $P$ is a Borel subgroup of $PGL(2)$) is irreducible. However, contrary to the classical case it turns out that these restrictions are not isomorphic to the "standard" irreducible cuspidal representation of $P(K)$. In the Appendix we propose a notion of cuspidality for smooth representations of the group $H(K)$ for an arbitrary split reductive group $H$.

papers.title: Relationship between generic Hecke algebra modules and $0$-Hecke algebra modules
papers.abstract: Let $H_{R,a}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ be the Hecke algebra over a principal ideal domain $R$ with parameter $a\in R$. The representation theories of $H_{\mathbb{C}(v^{1/2});v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ and $H_{\mathbb{C};0}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ differ substantially and have largely been studied independently. In this paper, we relate the categories of finitely generated modules of these two algebras through specialization functors from the category of finitely generated $H_{\mathbb{C}[v^{1/2}];v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$-modules. We first investigate the fundamental properties of these functors concerning dimensions, essential surjectivity, and characters. We then construct $H_{\mathbb{C}[v^{1/2}];v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$-modules which, through these functors, provide connections between skew Specht modules of $H_{\mathbb{C}(v^{1/2});v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ and $0$-Hecke skew Specht modules of $H_{\mathbb{C};0}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$, and between Kazhdan--Lusztig cell modules of $H_{\mathbb{C}(v^{1/2});v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ and dual plactic class modules of $H_{\mathbb{C};0}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$. Both families of $H_{\mathbb{C};0}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$-modules are closely related to regular Schur labeled skew shape posets. We further explore how specialization functors relate the Frobenius characteristic to the quasisymmetric characteristic and connects the branching rules for skew Specht modules with those for $0$-Hecke skew Specht modules. Finally, we use the established connection with Kazhdan--Lusztig cell modules to obtain a result on the classification of dual plactic class modules up to isomorphism.

papers.title: A Non-graded Koszul Duality and Its Applications
papers.abstract: Let \(\Lambda\) be a finite-dimensional Koszul algebra with Koszul dual \(\Lambda^!\). We establish derived Koszul dualities at the level of bounded derived categories, both in the graded setting \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(\Lambda\textup{-gmod})\) and in the ungraded setting \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(\Lambda\textup{-mod})\). We first prove a graded derived Koszul duality for every finite-dimensional Koszul algebra, with no Noetherian or coherence assumptions on the Koszul dual. We then show that the bounded derived category \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(\Lambda\textup{-mod})\) can be reconstructed from the graded theory as the triangulated hull of an orbit category. This yields a genuinely non-graded derived Koszul duality. We further establish singular and dg refinements of these dualities. For Iwanaga--Gorenstein Koszul algebras, this gives a stable Koszul duality for graded Gorenstein-projective modules and their ungraded counterparts, providing a non-graded form of the Bernstein--Gel'fand--Gel'fand correspondence. As applications, we obtain new descriptions of the bounded derived categories \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(\mathcal{O}_{\lambda})\) for all integral blocks of category \(\mathcal{O}\), including singular blocks, which are non-graded counterparts of the Koszul dualities of Beilinson, Ginzburg, and Soergel. We also establish analogous dualities for certain categories of perverse sheaves arising in geometric representation theory. Finally, we formulate conjectural descriptions of bounded derived and singularity categories of finite-dimensional graded algebras in terms of dg orbit categories.

papers.title: A note on finite length for $\mathrm{GL}_2$
papers.abstract: Let $p>2$ be a prime and $F/\mathbf{Q}_p$ be a finite extension. We prove that every admissible smooth mod $p$ representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$, with a central character, and satisfying a Casimir annihilation condition, has finite length.

papers.title: Non-factorisable Yangian Lax matrices through oscillators
papers.abstract: We construct oscillator realisations of Yangian Lax operators in type $A$, with particular interest in non-factorisable operators associated with prime snake modules. Our construction applies to finite-dimensional skew representations of $Y(\mathfrak{gl}_n)$. We prove that these representations are generated by the tensor vacuum in suitably ordered tensor products of oscillator representations. Their Lax operators are obtained by restricting the corresponding products of linear oscillator Lax operators to these submodules. We determine the vacuum eigenvalues and Drinfeld polynomials, and give a determinant formula for the dimensions directly in terms of the highest loop weights. A $21$-dimensional example illustrates the construction, including an explicit basis and a transfer-matrix identity.

papers.title: On the continuity of the geometric side of the twisted trace formula
papers.abstract: We establish the continuous extension of the geometric side of the twisted trace formula to a natural space of test functions, which are not necessarily compactly supported, for reductive algebraic groups. The continuity of the geometric side of the (untwisted) Arthur trace formula was established by Finis--Lapid. Subsequently, Parab generalized their result to the twisted trace formula under a certain restriction on the truncation parameter and an additional assumption. In this paper, we remove his restriction and assumption, and prove the continuous extension for the twisted trace formula. We also give a revised form of Parab's decay estimate for the geometric side.

papers.title: On $\iota$Quiver (BPS) Algebras and (Strict) Partitions
papers.abstract: We consider the $\iota$quiver algebras of split type associated with the quiver BPS algebras of affine type A. They are supposed to give twisted affine Yangians and (elliptic) $\iota$quantum toroidal algebras that could possibly arise from D-branes on $\mathbb{C}\times\mathbb{C}^2/\mathbb{Z}_n$ with orientifolds. We mention some properties of these algebras, such as the minimalistic presentations in the rational cases and the coideal structures. We also investigate how one might identify these algebras from the quiver theories with orientifold actions. Moreover, we discuss some representations with combinatorial bases of these algebras. In particular, the algebras with $n=1,2$ in certain limits of the parameters have representations labelled by (coloured) strict/symmetric partitions, which in the case of $n=1$ recovers the known BPS counting of certain theories.

papers.title: Two categorifications of the Kekul\'e relations
papers.abstract: We give new relations in the kernel of the foam evaluation. As a consequence we obtain categorifications of all the Kelul\'e relations introduced by Morrison. Along the way, we discover an equivalent set of relations for which we provide categorifications as well.

papers.title: Beyond Finite Dimensions: Duflo-Serganova Cohomology, the Formal Superdimension, and a Kac-Wakimoto Theorem for Unitarizable Supermodules
papers.abstract: The main results of this manuscript are fourfold. First, we introduce relative holomorphic discrete series supermodules over basic classical Lie superalgebras $\mathfrak{g}$ and $\mathfrak{sl}(n\vert n)$. These are unitarizable highest weight supermodules whose $\mathfrak{g}_{\bar{0}}$-constituents are Harish-Chandra modules of relative holomorphic discrete series representations. We show that these are exactly the unitarizable highest weight supermodules whose globalizations have supermatrix coefficients square-integrable modulo the center. Second, we define the formal superdimension of a relative holomorphic discrete series supermodule as the parity-weighted sum of the formal dimensions of its $\mathfrak{g}_{\bar{0}}$-constituents. We show that it equals, up to sign, the value at zero of an $L$-packet supercharacter obtained by averaging over the Weyl group. Third, we prove a Kac-Wakimoto theorem for formal superdimension: it is nonzero if and only if the highest weight is maximally atypical. For integral highest weights, it equals the superdimension of a finite-dimensional simple supermodule with the same degree of atypicality. We realize these supermodules through derived Zuckerman functors. For nonintegral highest weights, it is computed by generalized Duflo-Serganova cohomology. Finally, to establish the Kac-Wakimoto conjecture, we develop the theory of generalized Duflo-Serganova cohomology for unitarizable supermodules. We prove that the cohomology of a unitarizable simple supermodule is unitarizable and either zero or simple.

papers.title: Kronecker Coefficients and Simultaneous Conjugacy Classes
papers.abstract: A Kronecker coefficient is the multiplicity of an irreducible representation of a finite group $G$ in a tensor product of irreducible representations. We define Kronecker Hecke algebras and use them as a tool to study Kronecker coefficients in finite groups. We show that the number of simultaneous conjugacy classes in a finite group $G$ is equal to the sum of squares of Kronecker coefficients, and the number of simultaneous conjugacy classes that are closed under elementwise inversion is the sum of Kronecker coefficients weighted by Frobenius-Schur indicators. We use these tools to investigate which finite groups have multiplicity-free tensor products. We introduce the class of doubly real groups, and show that they are precisely the real groups which have multiplicity-free tensor products. We show that non-Abelian groups of odd order, non-Abelian finite simple groups, and most finite general linear groups do not have multiplicity-free tensor products.

papers.title: Shifted quantum affine symmetric pairs: finite presentations and graded coideal structures
papers.abstract: Shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras were recently introduced as a trigonometric analogue of shifted twisted Yangians, whose truncations are expected to quantize fixed point loci in generalized affine Grassmannian slices. They are defined via a loop presentation with infinitely many generators and relations. In this paper, we consider anti-dominantly shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras of simply-laced split type. Our main result is a construction of a finite presentation \`{a} la Levendorskii. We apply it in type $\mathsf{A}$ to construct an embedding of a shifted quantum symmetric pair algebra into the corresponding shifted quantum affine algebra, yielding a graded coideal structure.

papers.title: On two-dimensional affine Springer fibres
papers.abstract: We extend results of Spaltenstein on irreducible components of two-dimensional usual Springer fibres in reductive groups of simply lace type to the case of two-dimensional affine Springer fibres associated to loop groups. One of our methods is to relate these affine Springer fibres with certain subsets of the affine Weyl group.

papers.title: Spherical functions of the quantum symmetric pair of type FII
papers.abstract: We prove Schl\"osser's conjecture relating quantum FII spherical functions to Askey--Wilson polynomials for equal left and right coideal parameters and determine the corresponding radial operator. An explicit transport formula gives the shifted restrictions for arbitrary nonzero parameters.

papers.title: Classification of ${\rm GL}_1(D)\times {\rm GL}_{n-1}(D)$-distinguished representations
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be a quaternion division algebra over a non-Archimedean local field $F$ of characteristic zero. We prove the conjecture of Dagar, Sharma, and Verma classifying irreducible smooth representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(D)$ distinguished by $\mathrm{GL}_1(D)\times\mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(D)$ for $n>2$. These are precisely the trivial representation and the irreducible normalized parabolic inductions $\one_{n-2}\times\tau$, where $\tau$ is an infinite-dimensional irreducible representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(D)$ distinguished by $\mathrm{GL}_1(D)\times\mathrm{GL}_1(D)$. The proof combines a choice of cuspidal inducing factor with orbit conditions and multisegment methods.

papers.title: Cotorsion pairs in $\eta$-extensions with applications to $\theta$-extension rings and tensor rings
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal B$ be an abelian category with enough projective and injective objects, and let $\mathcal B\ltimes_\eta F$ be an $\eta$-extension of $\mathcal B$ with $\eta$ associative. Given a cotorsion pair $(\mathcal X, \mathcal Y)$ in $\mathcal B$, we show that the cotorsion pair $(\Delta(\mathcal X),\Delta(\mathcal X)^\perp)$ exists for arbitrary associative $\eta$, removing the square-zero assumption $F^2=0$ from Hu's construction. When $(\mathcal X, \mathcal Y)$ is hereditary, the heredity of $(\Delta(\mathcal X),\Delta(\mathcal X)^\perp)$ is characterized by the first left derived functor of a canonical defect functor $\delta$. We also remark that Hu's construction and hereditary result for the cotorsion pair $({}^\perp U^{-1}(\mathcal Y), U^{-1}(\mathcal Y))$ remain valid without the nilpotence assumption on $\eta$. Under nilpotence hypotheses, we establish a completeness criterion for $(\Delta(\mathcal X),\Delta(\mathcal X)^\perp)$ using the Beligiannis radical functor $\mathfrak r$. And we also provide a completeness criterion for $({}^\perp U^{-1}(\mathcal Y), U^{-1}(\mathcal Y))$ if $\mathcal B\ltimes_\eta F$ has enough injective objects. We give sufficient conditions for their coincidence. Dual results are obtained for $\zeta$-coextensions. Finally, we specialize the theory to $\theta$-extension rings and tensor rings, where the abstract conditions admit explicit module-theoretic descriptions.

papers.title: Homomorphisms between Weyl modules for $\mathrm{GL}_3$ in characteristic $2$
papers.abstract: We classify the homomorphism spaces between Weyl modules for the general linear group $\mathrm{GL}_3$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $2$. We prove that these spaces have dimension at most one and give an explicit recursive procedure that determines when they are nonzero and constructs generators in terms of semistandard tableaux. As a consequence, we determine the dimensions of certain homomorphism spaces between Specht modules in characteristic $2$.

papers.title: Spectral action in Betti metaplectic Langlands
papers.abstract: We construct the spectral action in the context of Betti metaplectic Langlands theory. More precisely, we prove that the category of twisted sheaves on $\text{Bun}_G$ with nilpotent singular support admits a canonical action by the symmetric monoidal category of quasicoherent sheaves on the moduli of twisted $H$-local systems, where $H$ is the metaplectic dual group. This confirms the Betti version of the conjecture of Gaitsgory--Lysenko, originally formulated in the de Rham setting under the name ``metaplectic vanishing conjecture". Given a symmetric monoidal category with suitable symmetry, we develop a categorical framework by introducing a notion of twisted factorization homology and studying its categorical action. We show that the category of quasicoherent sheaves on the moduli of twisted local systems can be realized as a twisted factorization homology. Using metaplectic factorizable Satake we further prove that the metaplectic Hecke action naturally fits into our categorical framework. Combining these results, we obtain the desired spectral action.

papers.title: Submatrices of character tables and centers of ordinary and queer q-Schur superalgebras
papers.abstract: We obtain bases of the centers of the ordinary $q$-Schur superalgebra $\mathcal{S}_q(m|n,r)$ and the queer $q$-Schur superalgebra $\mathcal{Q}_q(n,r)$ in terms of Casimir elements of the Hecke algebra $\mathcal{H}_r$ and the Hecke-Clifford algebra $\mathcal{H}_r^c$, respectively. The key step is to find an invertible submatrix of the character table of $\mathcal{H}_r$ or $\mathcal{H}_r^c$ whose column index set is the support of the corresponding $q$-tensor module appearing in Schur-Weyl duality: for $\mathcal{H}_r$ this is the set $H_{m,n}(r)$ of $(m|n)$-hook partitions of $r$, while for $\mathcal{H}_r^c$ this is the set $\mathrm{SP}_n(r)$ of strict partitions of $r$ of length $\leq n$. Unlike the case of ordinary $q$-Schur algebras, the submatrix formed by taking the row index set to be the same as the column index set need not be invertible. We determine that the row index set should be chosen as $H_{\min\{m,n\},\max\{m,n\}}(r)$ for $\mathcal{S}_q(m|n,r)$, and as the preimage of $\mathrm{SP}_n(r)$ under the Glaisher correspondence for $\mathcal{Q}_q(n,r)$.

papers.title: A Solution to the Birkhoff Problem
papers.abstract: For a commutative uniserial ring $R$ of length $n$ we describe the indecomposable objects in the monomorphism category of $R$ independent of the specific ring for $n\leq 5$ and only dependent on the residue field for $n = 6$. Thus, the classification problem for the monomorphism category of $\mathbb{Z}/p^6 \mathbb{Z}$ reduces to the known case of $\mathbb{F}_p[x]/(x^6)$, resolving the Birkhoff Problem.

papers.title: Gordan-Rankin-Cohen brackets on $1|n$-dimensional superstrings with a contact structure for $n\leq 6$
papers.abstract: The binary projectively $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$-invariant differential operators between spaces of weighted densities on the 1-dimensional manifold are called Gordan transvectants or Rankin-Cohen (GRC) brackets. For the two contact series (with an even and an odd ``time'' variable) on the supercircle or superstring of dimension $1|2$, we describe analogs of GRC brackets. We have discovered many new operators. For $\mathfrak{osp}(2|2)\subset\mathfrak{k}(1|2)$, the space of invariant binary operators of every given order is $2$-dimensional for all weights of the densities, not only for the weights considered so far. For $\mathfrak{pe}(2)\subset\mathfrak{m}(1)$, there are three independent binary operators of order $2$, not two. While classifying them, we correct an earlier result on the unary operators: the order-$2$ Bol operator over $\mathfrak{m}(1)$ is only one member of a $1$-parameter family invariant for all weights, which corrects Theorem 5.1 of arXiv:2110.10504. We correct earlier findings in the $1|3$-dimensional case and consider $\mathfrak{osp}_a(4|2)$-invariant (GRC) brackets in $1|4$-dimensional case, where the order-$2$ bracket is independent of the parameter $a$ and is invariant under the whole of $\mathfrak{k}(1|4)$. In the $1|5$-dimensional case, the analogs of Bol operators are odd, of order $5+2k$, where $k=0,1,2,\dots$, and so is the first GRC bracket of odd order, which is of order $5$. We also settle the exceptional case $\mathfrak{as}\subset\mathfrak{kas}\subset\mathfrak{k}(1|6)$.

papers.title: A characterisation of almost gentle algebras
papers.abstract: A finite-dimensional algebra over an algebraically closed field is gentle if and only if its trivial extension is special biserial. We prove the corresponding characterisation for almost gentle algebras, that is, an algebra over such a field is almost gentle if and only if its trivial extension is special multiserial, which answers a question of Green and Schroll. As a consequence, the property of having a special multiserial trivial extension is invariant under stable equivalence.

papers.title: Nazarov-Sklyanin Lax operators at higher rank
papers.abstract: We construct a rank-$m$ Nazarov-Sklyanin Lax operator for generalized Macdonald functions. The operator acts on the horizontal Fock module of quantum toroidal $\mathfrak{gl}_1$, extended by an auxiliary polynomial space with $m$ components. A geometric realization is given by the tensor product with the dual tautological line on the equivariant $K$-theory of a Hecke correspondence studied by Negut. The eigenbasis is indexed by an $m$-tuple of partitions and an addable corner, whose content is the eigenvalue. We give an anti-normal factorization and prove that the Lax operator is self-adjoint for the transported Euler pairing. With unit framing weight, the rank-one specialization recovers the Nazarov-Sklyanin factorization. We then show that the Lax operator is conjugate to the companion matrix of a projected q-Miura operator of the deformed $W$-algebra of type $\mathfrak{gl}_m$. This also gives an explicit presentation of the $K$-theory of the Hecke correspondence.

papers.title: Non-tempered GGP conjecture for classical groups: the Bessel case
papers.abstract: In their recent paper, Gan, Gross and Prasad proposed a precise conjecture to describe the restrictions of representations of classical groups that lie in an L-packet of Arthur type. On top of local root numbers, the main notion considered is the relevance of two A-parameters. In this paper, we establish that the relevance of two A-parameters is sufficient for the existence of a Bessel period for a pair of representations in the associated L-packets. Moreover, such a pair is unique. We also prove the necessity of relevance for co-tempered A-parameters, and give several counterexamples in the general case.

papers.title: Folding of d-invariants via F-invariants with applications to quiver Hecke KR-modules
papers.abstract: The \(\de\)-invariant measures the interaction between two simple modules and controls the behavior of their convolution product. Using categorical interpretations of Cao's tropical and \(F\)-invariants, we establish folding formulas for the \(\Lambda\)-invariants between determinantial modules in arbitrary symmetrizable type and derive the corresponding \(\de\)-formula by symmetrization. We apply the \(\de\)-formula to quiver Hecke Kirillov--Reshetikhin modules and show that, in every finite type, their \(\de\)-invariants are completely determined by the coefficients of the symmetrized inverse \(t\)-quantized Cartan matrix. We obtain explicit formulas in all finite types, including closed formulas in the classical types \(A\), \(B\), \(C\), and \(D\).
